requirements.title: Detailed procedure descriptions use generic names and default procedure conventions
requirements.definition: In 17.11 detailed descriptions, procedure names are generic rather than specific; all functions are simple and all subroutines impure unless otherwise stated; dummy arguments have INTENT(IN) unless explicitly stated otherwise.

pending.procedure-names-generic: Source-control plan: import IEEE_CLASS as a generic name, probe IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE for default real and another real kind before each call, and call IEEE_CLASS only in supported branches; result assertions are owned by 17.11.2.
pending.functions-simple-by-default: Source-use plan: treat functions lacking an overriding Class statement as simple functions; for IEEE_CLASS the overriding elemental Class paragraph is registered separately.
pending.subroutines-impure-by-default: Source-use plan: treat subroutines lacking an overriding purity statement as impure; mode and status mutation fixtures must not assume purity.
pending.dummy-arguments-intent-in-by-default: Compile-time plan: for a procedure whose argument paragraph gives no explicit INTENT, pass a definable variable and assert the caller value remains unchanged only under that procedure result rule; argument mutation diagnostics remain interface-owned.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first, use conforming single-image programs, and assert only portable Clause 17 properties: named derived-type values, exact logical results, exact type/kind/rank characteristics, supported IEEE special-value classifications, exact representable arithmetic under the named support inquiry, or get/set round trips. Unsupported guarded branches are skips, not passes. Processor-dependent support availability, NaN payloads, exact halting mechanics, initial modes, approximation latitude, and IOMSG text are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Unnumbered argument and Restriction paragraphs do not create diagnostic obligations. Negative source mutations are non-diagnostic unless a future numbered rule requires rejection and the rejection is portably observable. Existing IEEE profile and formatting fixtures are recorded as nearby coverage only and are not rebound here.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 16 for source form, declarations, expressions, execution, modules, intrinsic assignment, I/O harnesses, formatting references, and generic intrinsic foundations. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: the remaining Clause 17 procedure descriptions, IEEE derived types and named constants, processor support inquiries, exception-flag semantics, rounding-mode semantics, and ISO/IEC 60559 terminology.

requirements.title: Floating-result elemental functions follow ISO special-value general rules
requirements.definition: For elemental IEEE_ARITHMETIC functions returning floating-point results, infinity and NaN arguments produce results consistent with ISO/IEC 60559 general rules, including limiting-case construction for infinities where a limit exists.

pending.floating-result-infinity-general-rule: Guarded branch plan: probe IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(0.0) and IEEE_SUPPORT_INF(0.0); supported branch evaluates IEEE_COPY_SIGN, IEEE_NEXT_UP, or another registered floating-result elemental function on an infinity and asserts the detailed result plus the limiting-case sign or class; unsupported branch records skip.
pending.floating-result-nan-general-rule: Guarded branch plan: probe IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(0.0) and IEEE_SUPPORT_NAN(0.0); supported branch evaluates a registered floating-result elemental function on IEEE_VALUE(0.0,IEEE_QUIET_NAN) and asserts the detailed NaN result through IEEE_IS_NAN; unsupported branch records skip.

requirements.title: Restriction-violating statements may appear in unexecuted program paths
requirements.definition: A program may contain statements that would violate a procedure Restriction paragraph upon execution.

pending.restriction-violating-statement-may-appe: Source-control plan: place an otherwise type-conforming IEEE_CLASS call in an unreachable branch guarded by a compile-time false logical while the executed path probes IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE before calling; the plan observes source admissibility only, never execution of an unsupported call.

Defines names in 17.11 descriptions as generic.
Example assumptions are illustrative and not normative.
Allows source presence of statements that would violate restrictions upon execution.
The note illustrates guarded use of support inquiries and is not a normative source unit.

review_rationale: Source registration for 17.6-17.10, 17.11, 17.11.1 and 17.11.2: halting, floating-point modes and status, exceptional values, IEEE arithmetic, the procedure summary and general rules, and IEEE_CLASS (batch214). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across three rounds; every IEEE effect is a guarded branch plan keyed to its own support inquiry, with exact 60559 results for infinity and subnormal operands. Source accounting only.
